/poll question: Reconsideration of Previously Adjudicated Complaints by Ulftadhg
text:
Author: Ulftadhg
Post: n/a (added from 2026-10-03 Senate agenda)
Doc: <https://docs.google.com/document/d/1C27uthF29qtIR3DFyaKtn9lnJ900-yyTnxWw0LxZFGI/edit?usp=sharing>
Summary:
- Bars a sitting Board of Directors from reopening, reconsidering, or relitigating a complaint already actioned and decided by a previous Board solely because the Board's membership has changed.
- A previously actioned complaint stays closed unless new evidence, information, or materially relevant data surfaces that was not available or reasonably obtainable at the time.
- Any request to reopen must specifically identify the new evidence, information, or materially relevant data relied upon.
- A change in Board membership, disagreement with the prior decision, a different interpretation of the same evidence, or a desire for a different outcome - each alone - is expressly insufficient grounds.
- Stated purpose: governance continuity and consistency across Board turnovers.
answer-1: Yes
answer-2: No
answer-3: Abstain
